summary: August Johan Bernet Kempers was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Leiden University. He directed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1936–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Kiel, Leipzig (under Georg Curtius), and Jena (under August Schleicher). He held posts at Göttingen, Jena, and served as professor at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.

August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald and Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, among others. He held academic posts at Bonn (1846), Charles University (1850, 1853), and Jena (1857).
August Sundin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

August Tholuck was a religious studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1820). He later held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1820–1826) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1877).

August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, and later under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Alexander Hamilton. He held professorships at the University of Jena and the University of Bonn.

Auguste Barth was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Strasbourg. He held a post at Collège Poincaré Saverne (~1856–1860) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1893–1916).
Auguste Comte was a philosopher who completed his studies at Lycée Joffre and École polytechnique (1814–1816).

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as director of Calcutta Madrasa (~1881–1899) and was Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society in 1891.

Aung San Suu Kyi, active in Tibetology and other fields, studied at Lady Shri Ram College, University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS University of London. She held a post at the United Nations (~1969–1971).

Awadh Kishore Narain specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, holding key academic posts at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Klein is a scholar of Japanology who studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994). He held posts at Bonn, the German Institute for Japanese Studies, and became a professor at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Axel Michaels is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and Kiel University. He held posts at Kiel, the Nepal Research Centre, the University of Bern, and Heidelberg University.
Ayako Nakamura works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg (attested 2009) and is attested as a research fellow there in 2026.

Ayinapalli Aiyappan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Madras. He served as superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1970).
Ayu Khandro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa.
Ayush Maheshwari is a scholar in computational studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and also held a post there.

Ayya Khema was a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and scholar who studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Ñāṇārāma. She served as a teacher at Buddha-Haus from 1989.
Azizah Nur is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst, Stanford (under Carl Bielefeldt), and Tibetan monastic institutions, later teaching at Institut des Hautes Études Tibétaines, Rabten Choeling, and UC Santa Barbara.
